argument:
The bear fairly identifies stretch, thin margins and uncertain stockpiling persistence. Those objections limit the entry case but do not negate the combination of comparable profit growth, positive FCF, modest leverage and independently supportive trend and news evidence.

A patient momentum allocation can recognize that relative strength without claiming the latest price is cheap. I concede a chase after the recent advance is less attractive than a controlled entry following consolidation. The bullish thesis is that delivered operating resilience can sustain the trend; it does not require temporary demand to persist indefinitely.
key_points: Comparable growth and cash generation underpin case
Patient entry rather than overbought chase
rebuttal_to_previous: Concede overbought entry and temporary-demand uncertainty; rebut the implication that the bullish case rests solely on stockpiling or a target increase.
